channel.title: CNN 5 Things
channel.description: Monday through Friday get up to speed on the biggest headlines of the day with 5 Things. On Saturdays, get a break for your ears with good news from 5 Good Things. And at noon and Sundays, we take you beyond the headlines to help make sense of what everyone is talking about in politics and beyond with One Thing.

item.title: Trump: FAA Equipment ‘Had a Heart Attack’
item.description: President Donald Trump weighs in on the nationwide ground stop that paralyzed air travel over the weekend – and the funding fight that lies ahead. Meanwhile, he is heading to Asia for a high-stakes summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Lindsay Clancy will be tried again for the murder of her children next year. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani says a controversial NYPD unit is being disbanded. And we’ll tell you some big names nominated for Grammy awards. Learn more about your ad choices. Visit podcastchoices.com/adchoices

item.title: How Low-Tech Spycraft May Have Helped Bring Down AI’s Top CEO
item.itunes:title: How Low-Tech Spycraft May Have Helped Bring Down AI’s Top CEO
item.itunes:author: CNN Podcasts
item.content:encoded:
In the wake of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s stunning resignation, many are asking how an alleged Chinese spy was able to reportedly get so close to one of Silicon Valley’s most influential executives. As President Donald Trump prepares for another trip to China this week, we talk to someone who used to investigate corporate espionage in Silicon Valley about how AI firms will need to rethink how they do security going forward. 

--- 

Guests: Phil Mattingly, CNN Chief Domestic Correspondent and Anchor & Frank Figluizzi, former FBI Assistant Director 

Host/Producer: David Rind 

Showrunner: Felicia Patinkin

item.title: The Grandpa Every NICU Baby Deserves
item.itunes:author: CNN Podcasts
item.content:encoded:
A grandfather who once feared the neonatal intensive care unit now calls it the place he belongs. Determined to challenge expectations of motherhood, ultrarunner Stephanie Case accomplished what no woman has before in Antarctica. A 15-year-old in Louisiana became the first child in the state to receive a groundbreaking gene therapy for sickle cell disease. A husband and wife in Birmingham, Alabama opened a grocery store in their neighborhood where residents had gone decades without one. Plus, more than 70 years after setting a transatlantic speed record, the SS United States made history again.  

Host/Producer: Krista Bo Polanco 

Producer: Eryn Mathewson, Ifeoma Dike 

Showrunner: Felicia Patinkin 

Editorial Support: Zach Goldbaum

item.title: FAA Issues Nationwide Ground Stop for All Flights
item.description: The FAA says all flights in the United States are grounded until further notice. Rescue efforts are underway after a tanker crashed into a river cruiser with more than 130 people onboard. The Supreme Court will decide if President Donald Trump can bar most asylum claims at the southern border. Trump is sending mixed messages on his approach to the Iran war. Major red flags surface after a deadly building collapse in Brooklyn. And, why prosecutors say the driver behind the wheel of pickup truck that killed two people won’t be charged. item.title: Bessent Kicks Off a Nvidia Blame Game
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent points the finger at Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over inaction towards the chip company run by the woman suspected of being a Chinese spy who reportedly had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Vice President JD Vance is reportedly reconsidering a 2028 presidential run. The global Microsoft outage appears to be resolving. Donald Trump Jr. is splitting with the popular prediction market Kalshi.
